name: Lagoon
notes: Sheltered coastal lagoons: mangroves and sea purslane on tropical lagoon shores, samphire/saltwort and reeds on temperate barrier lagoons (Venice, Baltic haffs), and dense seagrass meadows in the shallow water. Drawn on Caribbean and Indo-Pacific atoll lagoons, Mediterranean and Baltic lagoons; underwater species flagged.

canopy.name: Black mangrove
canopy.source: Avicennia germinans, Caribbean, Gulf of Mexico and W African lagoon shores, pneumatophore mats, 3-15 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Red mangrove
canopy.source: Rhizophora mangle, Neotropical and W African lagoon edges (R. stylosa in Indo-Pacific), stilt-rooted, 4-20 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Coconut palm
canopy.source: Cocos nucifera, atoll lagoon rims throughout the tropical Pacific and Indian Ocean, 15-30 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Tamarisk
canopy.source: Tamarix gallica, Mediterranean lagoon shores (Camargue, Venice littorals), feathery pink-flowered small tree 3-8 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Buttonwood
shrub.source: Conocarpus erectus, Caribbean/Florida/W Africa lagoon back-shores just above tide, shrub or small tree 2-10 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Shrubby seablite
shrub.source: Suaeda vera, Mediterranean and S Atlantic European lagoon shores and shingle, evergreen fleshy subshrub 0.5-1.2 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Beach naupaka
shrub.source: Scaevola taccada, Indo-Pacific atoll lagoon rims, mounding succulent-leaved shrub 1-3 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Sea purslane
ground.source: Sesuvium portulacastrum, pantropical lagoon mudflats and sand, succulent mat 5-20 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Perennial glasswort
ground.source: Sarcocornia fruticosa, Mediterranean and Atlantic lagoon salt marsh (Venice, Camargue), woody jointed samphire 20-100 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Common reed
ground.source: Phragmites australis, brackish Baltic and Black Sea lagoon (haff, liman) reedbeds, 2-4 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Saltmarsh rush
ground.source: Juncus maritimus, European and Mediterranean lagoon fringe, stiff dark-green rush tussocks 0.5-1.2 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Turtle grass
ground.source: underwater — Thalassia testudinum, Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico lagoon floors, dominant broad-bladed seagrass 20-50 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Neptune grass
ground.source: underwater — Posidonia oceanica, Mediterranean endemic seagrass meadows on sand, 30-100 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Dwarf eelgrass
ground.source: underwater — Zostera noltei, European Atlantic and Mediterranean lagoon shallows, fine-leaved intertidal seagrass 10-30 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Tape seagrass
ground.source: underwater — Enhalus acoroides, Indo-Pacific lagoons and reef flats, largest tropical seagrass with 1-1.5 m ribbon leaves — Wikipedia
